items.claim: The city-noun distinction correctly separates 11:10 from 11:11, and the row's undisclosed adjacent shared tokens are generic collection-wide vocabulary, not genuine cohesion.
items.evidence: Skeleton tokens confirm oshb:Prov.11.10 uses קריה and oshb:Prov.11.11 uses קרת for "city" -- distinct nouns, not a repeated catchword, supporting the row's rejection of an 11:10-11:11 cluster. The row does not disclose that 11:10 shares צדיקים with 11:9 and רשעים with 11:11, but a book-wide exact-token sweep (consonantal_index.json) shows both are generic antithetic-collection vocabulary (צדיקים in 21 verses book-wide; רשעים in 35 verses book-wide), not distinctive shared-content-token cohesion -- their non-disclosure does not weaken the single_proverb ruling.

items.claim: Mirrors 11:10's correct city-noun distinction; the row's undisclosed shared token with 11:10 is generic collection-wide vocabulary, not a meaningful catchword.
items.evidence: Skeleton confirms oshb:Prov.11.11's קרת is a distinct noun from oshb:Prov.11.10's קריה, both meaning "city" but not a repeated token -- the row's rejection of a cluster on that basis is byte-true. 11:10 and 11:11 do share רשעים ("the wicked"), undisclosed in the row, but a book-wide exact-token sweep returns רשעים in 35 verses across the antithetic collection, making it generic thematic vocabulary rather than distinctive cohesion evidence; the omission does not undermine the boundary call.

items.claim: The surety/collateral topic is correctly isolated from both neighbors; no shared skeleton token links 11:15 to 11:14 or 11:16.
items.evidence: A skeleton comparison of oshb:Prov.11.14, oshb:Prov.11.15, and oshb:Prov.11.16 (consonantal_index.json) finds zero shared content tokens across either adjacent pair, confirming no undisclosed cross-seam cohesion; the national-leadership (11:14) vs. surety (11:15) vs. honor/riches (11:16) topic separation the row argues is accurate, and rejecting a cluster with 11:16 for lacking shared vocabulary is the correct call.

items.claim: The rejected_alternative for a forward cluster with 11:19 addresses only sowing/reaping vocabulary and omits the verse's actual shared exact token with 11:19.
items.evidence: consonantal_index.json shows oshb:Prov.11.18 and oshb:Prov.11.19 both carry the exact token צדקה ("righteousness"); a book-wide exact-token sweep returns only 10 verses total (Prov.8.20, 11.18, 11.19, 12.28, 13.6, 14.34, 15.9, 16.31, 21.3, 21.21), and 11:18-11:19 is the sole adjacent pair among them -- a rarity/single-adjacent-pair profile comparable to the noun evidence (3 verses book-wide, one adjacent pair) this same writer used elsewhere in this span to justify a proverb_cluster ruling. The row's claim that 11:19 "does not pick up this verse's sowing/reaping vocabulary" is true on its own narrow terms but sidesteps the actual shared noun, leaving the real rival candidate untested rather than rejected on its merits.

items.claim: The row's rejected_alternative asserts 11:18 and 11:19 share no lexical catchword, but byte evidence shows both verses carry the identical rare exact token tsedaqah, directly contradicting the stated ground for the single_proverb ruling.
items.evidence: consonantal_index.json skeleton tokens for oshb:Prov.11.18 and oshb:Prov.11.19 both include צדקה as an exact standalone token (not a prefixed variant). A book-wide exact-token sweep returns exactly 10 verses total (8.20, 11.18, 11.19, 12.28, 13.6, 14.34, 15.9, 16.31, 21.3, 21.21), and 11:18-11:19 is the ONLY adjacent pair among them -- this directly contradicts the row's explicit claim of "no lexical catchword" and matches the rarity/single-adjacent-pair profile that this writer's own proverb_cluster ruling at Prov.11.25-Prov.11.26 relied on for a noun with only 3 book-wide occurrences. The granularity call for 11:18-11:19 needs re-examination against this undisclosed shared token rather than resting on a false premise of no shared vocabulary. Secondarily, the row's distributional note on the prefixed noun לחיים ('non-adjacent to its other occurrence at the Prov.10.16-Prov.10.17 cluster') omits a third book-wide occurrence at Prov.19.23 (exact-token sweep returns 4 verses total: 10.16, 10.17, 11.19, 19.23), understating the token's full distribution.

items.claim: The existential construction is correctly and carefully notated as an elided second occurrence rather than a literal repetition, and no undisclosed cross-seam catchword links 11:24 to either neighbor.
items.evidence: Skeleton for oshb:Prov.11.24 confirms only one written token of "there is" (יש), with the second clause's implied "there is" correctly parenthesized by the row as elided rather than literally present -- byte-accurate. The only token 11:24 shares with a neighbor is the particle אך, also present in 11:23, a two-letter restrictive particle (6 verses book-wide) that functions grammatically, not as a content-bearing catchword, so its non-disclosure is not a defect; the row's rejection of extension into the 11:25-11:26 pair on the absence of the blessing noun is correct.

items.claim: The row labels its 3-verse sweep the exact spelling of the blessing noun, but word-bound checking shows two of the three hits are prefixed forms, not the bare spelling; the digit and adjacency conclusion driving the cluster ruling are independently confirmed correct.
items.evidence: A book-wide skeleton substring sweep for ברכה does return exactly 3 verses (Prov.10.7, Prov.11.25, Prov.11.26), matching the row's cited digit, and 11:25-11:26 is confirmed the only adjacent pair among them -- the cluster's core evidentiary claim holds. But word-bound token checking shows only Prov.11.25 carries the literal unprefixed token ברכה; Prov.10.7 carries the prefixed form לברכה and Prov.11.26 carries the prefixed form וברכה -- a mixed bare-plus-prefix lexeme sweep, not the "exact spelling" the row names. The construct-state exclusion (a different noun form at Prov.10.22, Prov.11.11, Prov.24.25) is correctly and precisely distinguished, and the naming imprecision on the absolute-state count does not undermine the cluster's granularity conclusion.

items.claim: The tree-of-life/soul-winning imagery is correctly isolated from both neighbors; the shared token with 11:31 is generic collection-wide vocabulary, and the a-fortiori characterization of 11:31 is accurate.
items.evidence: Skeleton confirms no shared content token between oshb:Prov.11.30 and oshb:Prov.11.29 (household topic); 11:30 and 11:31 do share the token צדיק ("the righteous [one]"), undisclosed in the row, but a book-wide exact-token sweep returns צדיק in 34 verses, generic antithetic-collection vocabulary, not distinctive cohesion. The row's characterization of 11:31's hen...af ki construction as an a-fortiori conclusion is an accurate device reading, and the synthetic (non-adversative) classification of 11:30 itself is correct.
